sources.entry: OwnTracks Recorder ⚠ - Store and access data published by OwnTracks location tracking apps. GPL-2.0 C/Lua/deb/Docker

summary.one_liner: OwnTracks Recorder is a lightweight program that stores location data published by the OwnTracks apps (via MQTT or HTTP) in plain files and serves it through a REST API, WebSocket live map, and the ocat CLI.
summary.what_it_does: The Recorder subscribes to an MQTT broker or accepts OwnTracks JSON via HTTP POST, and writes the data into a file-based store with no external database required. It serves a built-in HTTP server with a REST API (JSON data at /api/0/), static pages, example views such as a last-position table and live map updated over WebSocket, and GeoJSON maps and tracks. The ocat command-line tool reads the store directly and outputs JSON, GeoJSON, CSV, GPX, XML, or raw formats, with filters for user, device, time range, and limit. It performs reverse-geocoding of coordinates (via OpenCage, Google, revgeod, or a Lua hook) with an LMDB cache, and can expire cached entries. Views let you share a restricted, time-limited slice of data via a small JSON file with optional digest authentication. Optional features include payload encryption, Lua hooks, and friends lists in HTTP mode.
use_cases: self-host a location history for OwnTracks phones
record and replay personal GPS tracks
share a limited time window of location with friends
export location data to GPX, CSV, or GeoJSON
show live device positions on a map
reverse-geocode location history into addresses and countries
how_to_run: Install from the OwnTracks package repository, or pull the Docker image from Docker Hub
Or build from source (see Building section of README)
Configure settings in /etc/default/ot-recorder (OTR_* variables) or via command-line options
Run ot-recorder with MQTT broker settings (OTR_HOST, OTR_PORT, OTR_TOPICS) or enable HTTP mode
Query data with ocat, e.g. ocat --last --user demo --device iphone
Open the built-in web server (default port 8083) to view the table and live map
notable: Stores data in plain files with no external database; LMDB is used only for the reverse-geo cache and named databases
ocat CLI reads the store directly and exports many formats including GPX and GeoJSON
Views give visitors a sandboxed, date-limited view of selected user/device data
Optional payload encryption and Lua hooks for customizing behavior
Built-in WebSocket live map that updates as new publishes arrive
caveats: The built-in HTTP server only speaks plain HTTP; the README says to put TLS and authentication in front (e.g. nginx, Apache, Caddy) before exposing it publicly
Packages are no longer built for Debian 10, 11, and 12; those users must compile from source
Reverse-geo lookups with Google or OpenCage require API keys and respect provider quotas
